nodes.summary: Let $f : \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}$ be twice continuously differentiable and let $c$ be a simple root of $f$: $f(c) = 0$ and $f'(c) \ne 0$. Then there exist $\delta > 0$ and a real constant $C$ with the following property. For every $x_0 \in (c - \delta, c + \delta)$ and every real sequence $(x_n)$ that starts at $x_0$ and satisfies $x_{n+1} = x_n - f(x_n) / f'(x_n)$ for all $n$, every $x_n$ lies in…
nodes.title: Local quadratic convergence of Newton's method

nodes.summary: Let $f : \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}$ be differentiable with $f(c) = 0$, let $x \in \mathbb{R}$, let $m > 0$ and let $K \ge 0$. If $f'$ is Lipschitz with constant $K$ on the closed interval between $c$ and $x$ and $m \le |f'(x)|$, then the Newton step from $x$ satisfies $\left| x - f(x) / f'(x) - c \right| \le (K / m)\, |x - c|^2$.
nodes.title: One-step error bound for Newton's method
